models.name: Model S — 3D solid-contact implicit FEA
models.what_it_computes: Per-screw axial and shear load fractions and plate force distribution using solid bone, plate, and screw geometries with nonlinear contact and friction

models.name: Model R — Beam–spring implicit FEA surrogate
models.what_it_computes: Per-screw axial load fractions using beam elements for plate/screws and nonlinear springs for screw–bone engagement

mechanisms.name: Four-point bending across a 10 mm diaphyseal gap
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Represents plate-dominant bending where screw axial force sharing governs construct stiffness and risk of localized screw overloading

mechanisms.name: Axial compression with 5 mm medial eccentricity
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Introduces combined compression–bending that shifts load to near-gap screws, a common worst-case clinical scenario

mechanisms.name: Pure torsion about the long-bone axis
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Produces screw group warping and differential load paths not captured by simple axial tests, relevant to twisting injuries and gait-induced torsion

deviation.detail: All factor scores are reported on a 0–7 Credibility Attainment Scale (CAS), where 0 = no evidence and 7 = comprehensive evidence sufficient for high-risk decisions.

expected_decision.outcome_source: The final decision is Not accepted for the stated context of use.
rationale_keywords: predefined acceptance criterion was not met

expected_context_of_use: The context of use for both models is to support down-selection of new plate configurations by predicting per-screw axial load fractions and plate force distribution for the three bench tests prior to physical testing.

spans: In four-point bending, the 80 mm support span and 40 mm load spacing were represented explicitly in Model S via contact between the plate and rigid anvil surfaces and, in Model R, via beam nodes constrained to the same geometric positions.

In four-point bending, this representation captured the principal load path with end constraints approximating platen contacts, and its numerical behavior was stable with small changes in outputs under refinement.
findings.span: In four-point bending, the 80 mm support span and 40 mm load spacing were represented explicitly in Model S via contact between the plate and rigid anvil surfaces and, in Model R, via beam nodes constrained to the same geometric positions.

spans: For Model R, the axial spring parameters were identified from prior testing of isolated screws under axial displacement in the same surrogate polymer.

The springs exhibit piecewise linear stiffness profiles identified from prior calibrations that fit force–displacement data from isolated screw pull-up and unloading experiments in the same surrogate material.
findings.span: For Model R, the axial spring parameters were identified from prior testing of isolated screws under axial displacement in the same surrogate polymer.

spans: For Model R, beam element checks included recovery of exact solutions for bending and torsion of prismatic members, with tip deflections and twist matching textbook values to within machine precision for linear cases.
Spring assemblies were verified using a series configuration test and against a piecewise linear target response, ensuring that the intended axial stiffness segments were realized.
findings.span: For Model R, beam element checks included recovery of exact solutions for bending and torsion of prismatic members, with tip deflections and twist matching textbook values to within machine precision for linear cases.
